Sure, here are two hints for the given problem:

Hint 1: Consider the properties of an OLS model. Remember that the Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) method aims to minimize the sum of the squared differences between the observed and predicted values. This means that the fitted model will have certain characteristics that are inherent to OLS.

Hint 2: Think about the implications of having a unique optimal solution in the context of OLS. A unique solution suggests that the model parameters are determined in such a way that they minimize the error for the given data set. Consider how this affects the relationship between the predicted values (\(\hat{y}_i\)) and the actual outcomes (\(y_i\)).
